subject: Food Science
title: Smoke Points
description: A quick, practical guide to Smoke Points.

hook.text: Heat olive oil too much and it smokes, turning bitter with toxic compounds. Every oil has a breaking point.

buildup.text: The smoke point is the temperature where oil breaks down, releasing acrolein—a noxious, eye-stinging gas.

discovery.text: Refined avocado oil smokes at 271°C. Extra virgin olive oil at 190°C. Butter at just 175°C.

twist.text: Refining removes impurities that lower smoke points. Refined oils handle higher heat but lose flavor.

climax.text: Deep frying at 190°C needs oils with high smoke points. Using the wrong oil fills your kitchen with fumes.

punchline.text: Right oil, right heat. That's the rule of smoke points.

quiz.question: What happens when oil exceeds its smoke point?
options: It breaks down and releases toxic compounds like acrolein
